objective_text.T68.01.b: Derive head<count/capacity invariants, occupied logical slots and output ownership. Compare generated specialization with Rust generic/associated-type obligations and show a mismatched ring/element instantiation diagnosed by C. Explain why a template include guard would silently suppress the second instantiation and why internal macro names can collide.

Compile and link two translation units using declarations to detect accidental multiple definitions; record generated symbol count and text size separately from handwritten equivalents under the same capacity/failure contract.
objective_text.T68.01.d: Instantiate a ring of owning objects with fallible clone/drop callbacks. Derive rollback on failed push and destruction order on clear; compare monomorphized and erased implementations with equal semantics and measured code growth.

sets.title: Derived equality, hashing and shrinking law counterexamples

objective_text.T68.07.a: Explain the equality-implies-equal-hash law, why cached/nonsemantic fields must be excluded consistently, and what deterministic generation plus shrinking establishes and leaves unproved.
objective_text.T68.07.b: Prove reflexivity/symmetry/transitivity obligations separately from hashing and collisions. Specify FNV parameters and unsigned64 wrap; this is not a cryptographic integrity claim. The shrinking order finds a local minimum under decrement moves, not necessarily a globally simplest witness for arbitrary nonmonotone predicates. Callback/context must remain live, deterministic and side-effect controlled.

Inject a deliberately wrong equality/hash callback through the learner testing.faults adapter and retain a minimized witness; explain why equal hashes do not imply equal keys.
objective_text.T68.07.d: Add an allocation-failing string owner and generators for operation traces. Shrink while preserving preconditions and the same failure class; compare bytewise, semantic and normalized-text equality contracts before deriving hashes.

sets.title: Declarative build graphs and deterministic table generation

objective_text.T68.10.a: Derive build ordering separately from action invalidation, identify hidden inputs, and explain why a content key is only as complete and collision-resistant as its declared input model.
objective_text.T68.10.b: Prove Kahn-style readiness and termination, show how dependency content propagates into consumers, and distinguish source identity from timestamp ordering. Compare Ninja explicit/implicit/order-only dependency semantics and command-line rebuild tracking. The educational FNV key is not collision-resistant; require full input equality or a suitable cryptographic digest before any untrusted shared cache use.
objective_text.T68.10.c: Run metaprog.buildgraph and independent Python topological/hash reconstruction. Kill omitted-configuration and omitted-dependency-key mutants. Compile/run the generated C table consumer, permute input storage without changing logical IDs, and inject a missing implicit dependency to demonstrate stale generated metadata.
objective_text.T68.10.d: Introduce an incremental cache with toolchain, environment, include-file and schema dependencies. Simulate crashes during artifact publication and hash collisions; define atomic replacement and full-input verification. Compare a parallel scheduler only after establishing dependency and output ownership.
